connector: You finished the biography. Now meet the raid the way people first read about it in 1863. Two writers told the story of the same night on the Combahee River. One left out Harriet’s name. The other printed her own words. Read them one at a time, then ask what only each one tells you.

plate.alt: Harriet Tubman stands in a rowboat on the Combahee River at night, singing to families hurrying aboard while Union gunboats wait in the moonlight.
plate.credit: The Combahee River Raid, June 1863, the night all three sources describe.

a.raw: the raiders burned the barns the storehouses and the rice fields along the combahee river
a.fixed: The raiders burned the barns, the storehouses, and the rice fields along the Combahee River.
a.why: Capital T starts the sentence; commas after barns and storehouses separate the three things in the list; capital C and R on Combahee River; a period ends it.

b.raw: families carried baskets bundles and babies down to the riverbank
b.fixed: Families carried baskets, bundles, and babies down to the riverbank.
b.why: Capital F starts the sentence; commas after baskets and bundles separate the three items, including the one before and; a period ends it.

fill1.h1: Goods carried from one place to another. Which prefix means across?
fill1.why: trans- means across: trans + portation = carrying across.

fill2.h1: Something that happens among many countries. Which prefix means between?
fill2.why: inter- means between: inter + national = between nations.

fill3.h1: A boat that travels under the sea. Which prefix means under?
fill3.why: sub- means under: sub + marine = under the sea.

fill4.h1: Something beyond what nature can do. Which prefix means above or beyond?
fill4.why: super- means above or beyond: super + natural.

notes.wgrd: Read one account at a time. Say the event in your own words. Then list what only each account tells you.
vocab: Brave and heroic, especially in a noble cause.
A place where food and supplies are stored, especially for an army.
The Confederate states; the land of the rebellion.
During the Civil War, enslaved people who escaped to Union lines.
notes.wordParts: Prefixes that tell where: trans- = across, inter- = between, sub- = under, super- = above or beyond: transportation, international, submarine, supernatural.
notes.grammar: Commas in a series: put a comma after each item in a list of three or more, including before and. She packed bread, cheese, and a knife.
notes.spelling: Some words sound alike but mean different things. Affect is the action, effect is the result. It’s means it is; its shows belonging. Their means belonging to them, there is a place, they’re means they are. Accept means take; except means leave out.

why.t: Harriet’s mother finished a patchwork quilt in Chapter 2, and all year the word-parts game sewed patches like hers. The quilt was finished last week. This week you sew its border with four prefixes that tell where: trans- (across), inter- (between), sub- (under) and super- (above).

wordgame.winDay: Four border patches are sewn in.
wordgame.win: Four border patches are sewn in. trans- = across, inter- = between, sub- = under, super- = above.

read.label: Marcus · before you read the sources

transcripts.welcome: Hey, it’s Marcus. You finished Freedom Train, but we’re not done with Harriet. This week you read the Combahee River Raid the way people first read it, in 1863. Today’s question: why does it matter who tells a story?
transcripts.read: Read Source A all the way through, then Source B. Don’t jump back and forth yet. One writer never says her name. The other lets her talk. On my tours, this is where people get quiet. Notice what each one gives you that the other can’t.
transcripts.morphology: Some word parts tell you where. Trans means across. Inter means between. Sub means under. Super means above or beyond. Put one in front of a word, and the word knows where it’s going. Find the part that tells where, then sew the border patch.

virtue.title: Her own words
virtue.intro: In Source B, Harriet Tubman calls the people she helped free “seven hundred and fifty-six head of their most valuable livestock, known up in your region as ‘contrabands.’” She is using the slaveholders’ way of talking about people, on purpose.
virtue.line: Write one sentence: What is Harriet really saying about freedom?
virtue.name: freedom
